correctness.rationale: For a nilpotent triangular product, maximal nilpotency index equals the matrix dimension precisely when every first-superdiagonal entry is nonzero: the unique possible nonzero entry of its penultimate power is their product. The compatible diagonal strings consist exactly of an initial run of type L followed by a run of R, optionally separated by one Z. Counting those strings with diagonal-value weights and using the independence of free offdiagonal matrix entries proves the formula in all dimensions and finite fields. Direct pair enumeration over the six stated prime-field cases and separately coded three-state word counts reproduce numerical examples; this finite evidence is not the general proof.

value.rationale: Nilpotency index measures the largest Jordan block and the extremal behavior within the nilpotent-product event studied in current finite-ring research. The theorem determines a meaningful natural stratum over all matrix dimensions and finite fields, exact factor-pair counts, and a limiting discrepancy from the uniform nilpotent-matrix law. It is not a substitute parameter or an isolated small-table recomputation. The full Jordan-type distribution remains open within this work.
